stories.title: Elon Musk says many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Jensen Huang
stories.summary: On X on Saturday, Musk wrote that many of Nvidia's supply deals were "a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract" and that without Huang "at least some of those critical deals will be lost". He says he is signing a petition to reinstate Huang, which its organisers say passed 80,000 signatures.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Carbon tops the MathArena math leaderboard, at about 15 times GPT-6.1 Sol's cost
stories.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon scored 85.4% on MathArena, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 (82.8%) and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol (80.6%), the first non-OpenAI model on top in a while. With MathArena's settings it costs about 15 times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol ($15.70 vs $1.07).

stories.title: Siddhartha Mukherjee: AI cuts early drug discovery from nearly eight years to months
stories.summary: At the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, the oncologist and Manas AI co-founder said AI is compressing early-stage drug discovery from nearly eight years to three or four months, but doesn't yet change the cost of trials or "the regulatory clock".

stories.title: Anthropic's seven co-founders could each be worth about $17-18 billion after its IPO
stories.summary: Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders holds about 240 million class A shares (about 1.4%), CNBC reports; at the expected $70-78 a share, each stake would be worth $17-18 billion. Trading is expected to start on Nov 19.

stories.title: UK Treasury is reportedly wargaming an AI tax in case of widespread job losses
stories.summary: The Telegraph reports that Treasury officials are analysing how AI job losses could cut income tax and National Insurance receipts, with options discussed including a tax on owning or operating AI and a "robot services tax". The planning is at an early stage and decisions are some way off.

predictions.note: The Telegraph reports the UK Treasury is studying how AI job losses could erode income tax and National Insurance, with AI taxes among the options.
Options reportedly discussed include a tax on owning or operating AI and a 'robot services tax'; decisions are some way off.

stories.title: Trump and Xi are set to discuss an AI crisis hotline at APEC in Shenzhen
stories.summary: According to AFP, the two presidents agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be worked out at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19.

stories.title: Karnataka brings AI education to Class 9 in 1,800 government high schools
stories.summary: India's Karnataka state is introducing AI education for Class 9 students in 1,800 government high schools in the 2026-27 school year, through its Department of School Education and Literacy.

stories.title: A CSIRO AI trained on everyday photos confirms the ring in the first black hole image
stories.summary: A CSIRO team in Perth re-imaged the M87* black hole, 55 million light years away, with an AI model trained on everyday pictures such as animals and cars rather than astronomy, and confirmed the ring shape a rival group had questioned. The work was published in Nature.

stories.title: About 6,000 people march in Edinburgh against AI data centres
stories.summary: An estimated 6,000 people marched down the Royal Mile to the Scottish Parliament on Saturday, with placards such as "We cannae drink data". 28 data centre proposals totalling 8.9GW are queued for Scotland's grid, over twice its winter peak demand.

predictions.note: About 6,000 marched in Edinburgh against AI data centres, as 28 proposals totalling 8.9GW, over twice Scotland's winter peak, queue for its grid.

stories.title: Four nonprofits sue OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to freeze frontier AI
stories.summary: Public Citizen, the Heat Initiative, Irreplaceable Education Fund and the Alliance for Secure AI filed a complaint in San Francisco Superior Court seeking an injunction against systems more capable than each company's best as of the filing date, Nov 12. These are allegations; no court has ruled.

stories.title: Tesla invites some buyers to order a Cybercab for personal use, at $29,990 plus $299 a month
stories.summary: The steering-wheel-free two-seater costs $29,990 plus a mandatory $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription, with a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and works only in supported service areas. Musk called the subscription too high, saying it should be about $115 a month.

stories.title: Runway releases Praxis-1, an open robot-control model built on video AI
stories.summary: Runway's Praxis-1 is open under the Apache 2.0 licence. On a real robot arm, across ten tasks with ten tries each, it succeeded 88 times to FLUX 3 Action's 80, in Runway's own tests, which have not been independently verified.

transcript.t: It's Sunday, November 15, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Let's catch you up on the last 24 hours in superintelligence.
Today's about the human touch.
Elon Musk says Nvidia's big deals were a handshake with Jensen Huang.
Without him, Musk warns, some of those deals will be lost.
Meanwhile, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon just took first place on a tough math leaderboard.
Anthropic's Claude came second. OpenAI, the long-time leader, slipped to third.
It isn't cheap, though: about fifteen times the cost per run.
In New Delhi, cancer doctor Siddhartha Mukherjee said AI cuts early drug discovery from eight years to a few months.
But trials, he said, still run on the regulator's clock.
Now, the people.
Anthropic's seven co-founders could soon be worth about $17 billion each.
Britain's Treasury is reportedly war-gaming a tax on AI, in case it takes too many jobs.
Next week, Trump and Xi are set to talk about a hotline for AI emergencies.
And in India, Karnataka is adding AI classes for ninth graders in 1,800 public schools.
This week in Perth, a CSIRO team checked the first-ever black hole photo with an AI trained on cats and dogs.
It had never seen a black hole, so it couldn't be biased. It found the same ring.
The catch? In Edinburgh, about 6,000 people marched against giant AI data centres.
And four nonprofits are suing to freeze AI at this week's level.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Back to the machines. Tesla's inviting some buyers to own a Cybercab, with no steering wheel.
It's $29,990, plus $299 a month. Even Musk calls that too high.
This week, Runway turned a video AI into a robot brain, and gave it away free.
That's the human touch. Machines keep getting smarter, but trust still starts with a handshake.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
All of that, in one day. And the days keep getting bigger.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
Go build something. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
